accepted_checkpoints.acceptance_scope: The unified Pedido editing and client change-approval design is accepted, with four binding amendments that the contract now canonicalizes as ratified rulings in section U13. (1) CLIENT PEDIDO DATE: the Client MAY provide data_pedido during initial Pedido creation through the existing creation flow, which is not altered; after the Pedido exists data_pedido is read-only to the Client, and both salvar_pedido_cliente and solicitar_alteracao_pedido reject it. The R1 recommendation to remove the creation control is NOT adopted. (2) STRUCTURAL CHANGES AND EXISTING OPs: a structural item change is changing modelo_id, changing metros, inserting an item or removing an item. While no related OP exists these may be applied; once ANY related OP exists, in ANY status including simulada and cancelada, they are refused by the generic administrative save, by client submission and by approval. Approval confirmation is NOT an override and no parameter unlocks it. The R1 graded A-E impact ladder, its level-C impact confirmation and its level-D metres reconciliation are WITHDRAWN in full. Header fields, general observation and item observation remain editable by lifecycle, and production priority keeps definir_prioridade_pedido as its only owner with its existing impact confirmation. (3) ADMINISTRATIVE TRANSACTIONAL OWNER: salvar_pedido_admin(p_pedido_id, p_base_revisao, p_header, p_itens, p_prioridade, p_confirmar_impacto) is added and is atomic. (4) APPROVAL FAILURE OWNERSHIP: an expected validation refusal returns a stable identifier, leaves the request pendente and changes no live row; an unexpected failure during the application stage is rolled back by a PL/pgSQL exception subtransaction and the outer transaction records falha_aplicacao with falha_identificador, preserving the immutable before-image. No frontend or direct-DML caller owns that transition. Also ratified without amendment: pedidos.status = confirmado as the acceptance boundary, prazo_entrega as the sole expected-delivery owner, prazo_desejado as dormant legacy unchanged in this phase, the justified hybrid request model, at most one pending request per Pedido, one pedidos.revisao concurrency owner, the compatibility redirect and eventual retirement of #/pedidos/<uuid>/itens, and the dedicated approval screen with modal use limited to the final confirmation.

A. OPTION SELECTED. Option A of PEDIDO-ITEM-MENTION-OBSERVATION-UX-DESIGN-R1 is accepted. The administrative Pedido item table no longer exposes an editable per-item Observation column. The normal administrative observation-writing surface is the Pedido-level general observation field. B. ADMINISTRATIVE SURFACES. The decision applies to #/pedidos/novo and #/pedidos/<uuid>/editar. It does not apply to the client Pedido creation or editing surfaces in this phase. C. ITEM TABLE. Seven columns: Img, Tipo, Modelo, Cores, Largura, Metragem, Acoes. Approved target layout GRID_COLS "60px .70fr 1.45fr 1.15fr .80fr .90fr 92px" with a 790px minimum row and table content width. The Observation column is removed. Document-level horizontal overflow remains prohibited and the item table keeps local horizontal scrolling where required. D. ADMIN ADD-ITEM MODAL. The administrative detailed Adicionar item modal remains part of the accepted dual entry contract and is neither removed nor replaced. Its per-item observation input is retired from the administrative flow. The modal continues to collect the actual item identity and quantity fields, and must not create an item observation that becomes invisible immediately after confirmation. E. GENERAL OBSERVATION. The visible administrative field is identified as "Observacoes gerais". It continues to persist through pedidos.observacao. It remains editable in every non-terminal lifecycle state allowed by the existing Pedido rules, including when structural item controls are locked due to production linkage. F. MENTION ACTION. Each administrative item row receives one discreet mention action inside Acoes, before the destructive Remove action. Approved control: @ icon; canonical owner window.actionButton; canonical 30x30 action target; non-destructive neutral/accent treatment; title "Mencionar item {n} nas observacoes gerais"; accessible label containing the readable item identity; disabled when no model is selected; available when structural controls are locked; absent or disabled in terminal read-only rendering. G. INSERTED TEXT. The exact reference format is "@Item {1-based position} — {modelo} · {cor_1}/{cor_2} · {largura}: ", for example "@Item 3 — Noite · KRAFT/CRU · 2,10 m: ". Rules: no UUID; no pedido_item_id; no database identifier; do not include item metragem; use the current local item state and model projection; format width in pt-BR; leave the caret after the trailing colon and space. H. TEXT INSERTION. On activation: insert at the current selection/caret if the general observation field has an active usable selection, otherwise append at the end; add a newline before the mention when needed; focus the general observation textarea; place the caret after the colon and space; update the existing field state through its normal input path; autosize and bring the field into view when necessary; do not show a large toast for this local action. Repeated clicks deliberately insert repeated references. Deduplication and navigation to an earlier mention are prohibited. I. SNAPSHOT SEMANTICS. The mention is plain text and belongs to the operator written observation once inserted. The application must not automatically rewrite, renumber or remove an existing mention if the item model changes, the item order changes, the item is removed, or the Pedido is reloaded. Silent rewriting of operator-written text is prohibited. J. STRUCTURAL LOCK AND PERSISTENCE. Mentioning an item is non-structural.
